defmodule ReadaloudLibrary.Tasks.Dashboard do
  @moduledoc """
  The `/tasks` page in one struct. `load/0` reads every task table the
  framework knows about, partitions tasks by lifecycle status, sorts each
  partition, and presents each task as a `Row` with the contextual fields the
  UI needs (book title, chapter number, relative time). All DB work happens
  here so the LiveView's only job is to assign the result and re-render.
  """

  alias ReadaloudLibrary.{Repo, Tasks}

  defstruct active: [], completed: []

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          active: [Row.t()],
          completed: [Row.t()]
        }

  defmodule Row do
    @moduledoc """
    A single row in the tasks UI. Every field is computed at load time —
    rendering touches the DB only via the assigns it was given.
    """

    @enforce_keys [:task_id, :kind, :description]
    defstruct [
      :task_id,
      :kind,
      :description,
      :subtitle,
      :error_message,
      :relative_time,
      success?: false,
      failed?: false
    ]

    @type kind :: :audio | :import
    @type t :: %__MODULE__{
            task_id: integer,
            kind: kind,
            description: String.t(),
            subtitle: String.t() | nil,
            error_message: String.t() | nil,
            relative_time: String.t(),
            success?: boolean,
            failed?: boolean
          }
  end

  @doc """
  Load and present every task in the system. `now` is latched once so every
  row's `relative_time` is computed against the same instant.
  """
  def load(now \\ NaiveDateTime.utc_now()) do
    tasks = Enum.flat_map(Tasks.schemas(), &Repo.all/1)
    {active, terminal} = Enum.split_with(tasks, &Tasks.active?/1)

    active = Enum.sort_by(active, & &1.inserted_at, {:asc, NaiveDateTime})
    terminal = Enum.sort_by(terminal, & &1.updated_at, {:desc, NaiveDateTime})

    ctx = build_ctx(tasks, now)

    %__MODULE__{
      active: Enum.map(active, &present(&1, ctx)),
      completed: Enum.map(terminal, &present(&1, ctx))
    }
  end

  # --- private ---

  defp build_ctx(tasks, now) do
    chapter_ids =
      for %{__struct__: ReadaloudAudiobook.AudiobookTask, chapter_id: id} <- tasks,
          is_integer(id),
          do: id

    book_ids = for t <- tasks, is_integer(t.book_id), do: t.book_id

    %{
      chapter_numbers: ReadaloudLibrary.chapter_numbers_by_ids(chapter_ids),
      book_titles: ReadaloudLibrary.book_titles_by_ids(book_ids),
      now: now
    }
  end

  defp present(%{__struct__: ReadaloudAudiobook.AudiobookTask} = task, ctx) do
    description =
      case Map.get(ctx.chapter_numbers, task.chapter_id) do
        nil -> "Generating audio"
        n -> "Generating audio — Ch #{n}"
      end

    row(task, :audio, description, ctx)
  end

  defp present(%{__struct__: ReadaloudImporter.ImportTask} = task, ctx) do
    row(task, :import, "Importing #{Path.basename(task.file_path)}", ctx)
  end

  defp row(task, kind, description, ctx) do
    %Row{
      task_id: task.id,
      kind: kind,
      description: description,
      subtitle: Map.get(ctx.book_titles, task.book_id),
      error_message: task.error_message,
      success?: Tasks.completed?(task),
      failed?: Tasks.failed?(task),
      relative_time: relative_time(task.updated_at, ctx.now)
    }
  end

  defp relative_time(nil, _now), do: ""

  defp relative_time(dt, now) do
    diff = NaiveDateTime.diff(now, dt, :second)

    cond do
      diff < 60 -> "#{diff}s ago"
      diff < 3600 -> "#{div(diff, 60)}m ago"
      diff < 86_400 -> "#{div(diff, 3600)}h ago"
      true -> "#{div(diff, 86_400)}d ago"
    end
  end
end

## Checkpoint 5 — Re-read until quiet

Putting on the new-developer-with-autocomplete glasses.

### What `Tasks.` shows

```
Tasks.subscribe/0          ← LiveView subscribes to all task topics
Tasks.get/1                ← look up by id, struct or nil
Tasks.cancel/1             ← cancel by id
Tasks.clear_completed/0    ← bulk delete terminals
Tasks.schemas/0            ← framework's known task schemas
Tasks.start/1              ← lifecycle: → :processing
Tasks.complete/1, /2       ← lifecycle: → :completed
Tasks.fail/2               ← lifecycle: → :failed
Tasks.active?/1, terminal?/1, pending?/1, processing?/1, completed?/1, failed?/1
```

Every entry is a verb the consumer cares about. No leak of "audiobook" or "import" in any name. ✓

### What `Dashboard.` shows

```
Dashboard.load/0           ← whole page in one call
Dashboard.load/1           ← same, with explicit `now` for tests
Dashboard.Row.t/0          ← typespec for the row struct
```

Two callable surfaces and a type. ✓

### Obvious-mistake compile errors

- Pass `"abc"` to `Tasks.cancel/1` → `FunctionClauseError` from `is_integer(id)` guard. Loud. ✓
- Forget the `nil` clause for retry → `FunctionClauseError` on `Tasks.get/1` returning nil. The `nil` clause is in place. ✓
- Drop `:audio` to `:audiobook` in `Row.kind` typespec → dialyzer flags any pattern-match against the old atom. ✓
- New status enum value lands → no longer crashes render (the `cond` is gone). It silently appears in `:active` if `Tasks.active?` says so, in `:completed` otherwise — both partitions fall out of the predicate, so adding a status never breaks the page. ✓

### Itches I tried to surface and couldn't

- The struct-module-name dispatch in `Tasks.queue_for/1` and `Tasks.topics_for/1` is the F2 deferred concern. Reading it cold, the inline comment explains the cycle constraint. I'd still prefer the registry, but the user explicitly took it off the table.
- `Tasks.cancel/1` swallows the not-found case and returns `:ok`. A worker reading this might assume cancellation succeeded. I considered widening to `{:ok, task} | :not_found` but the only caller (the LiveView) discards the return and re-loads the dashboard. Stays.
- The retry dispatch in `tasks_live.ex` is the *only* place a consumer module-name appears in the LiveView. It's three pattern clauses, fully explicit, and self-documenting via the inline comment. This is the right shape *given the scope* — it stays until F2 lands.

I genuinely cannot name another itch. Loop terminates.

---

## Summary

| Change | File | Move(s) |
|--------|------|---------|
| New `Tasks.Dashboard` + `Dashboard.Row` typed structs | `apps/readaloud_library/lib/readaloud_library/tasks/dashboard.ex` (new) | 1, 2, 7 |
| Add `Tasks.subscribe/0`, `Tasks.get/1`, `Tasks.cancel/1`, `Tasks.clear_completed/0`, `Tasks.schemas/0` | `apps/readaloud_library/lib/readaloud_library/tasks.ex` | 1, 3 |
| Privatize `Tasks.broadcast/1` | same | 7 (surface) |
| Scope Oban-cancel query by queue (latent collision bug) | same | 7 |
| Remove `clear_completed_tasks/0` from `ReadaloudAudiobook` and `ReadaloudImporter` | both | 6 (dead) |
| Rewrite `TasksLive` — typed dashboard assign, single retry helper, strict `handle_info` pattern | `apps/readaloud_web/lib/readaloud_web_web/live/tasks_live.ex` | 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 9 |

**LiveView line count**: 287 → 175. **Public API for `/tasks`**: four `Tasks.*` verbs + `Dashboard.load/0`.

**Verification**:
- `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` — clean
- `mix format --check-formatted` — clean
- `mix credo --strict` — 0 issues across 83 files
- `mix test` — 77 tests, 0 failures
- `mix precommit` halts on the **same 4 pre-existing dialyzer warnings** in `test/support/conn_case.ex` (ExUnit macro internals); confirmed by `git stash -u` baseline run. My changes introduce no new dialyzer findings.
- e2e (`mix test.e2e`) **not run** — there's no `/tasks` page test today, and the VM provisioning cost (~2 min cold) wasn't justified for this refactor. Worth running before deploy if you want belt-and-suspenders.

**Fast-follows (out of scope, your call)**:
- **F1** — Privatize `ReadaloudAudiobook.failed_tasks_by_chapter/3`, `list_tasks_for_chapters/1`, `list_chapter_audio_for_chapters/1` (single same-module callers each).
- **F2** — Replace struct-module-name dispatch in `Tasks` with a registry (Move 4 full inversion), once a third task type appears.
- **F3** — Deploy. The local fix for the 500 — `1fad07d` — is already on `master` (ahead of origin by 1 + this refactor). `git push` + `colmena apply` ships it. The refactor is independent of the fix and can ship in the same deploy.

file.content:
---
name: readaloud test/commit/deploy/verify flow
description: End-to-end procedure for landing a code change in readaloud — test, commit, deploy via configs flake input, verify in browser.
type: reference
originSessionId: 23193cc2-0713-490e-8c51-0225ef558d27
---
The readaloud project deploys to pylon as a NixOS module via flake input from GitHub. The full loop:

**1. Test**
- `direnv exec . mix compile --warnings-as-errors` from project root — fast sanity check.
- For real tests: `direnv exec . env MIX_ENV=test mix test apps/<app>/test/<file>.exs`. Umbrella-root `mix test` is brittle (per-app DBs need migrations) — prefer per-file invocation. The library/reader tests fail under per-app `mix test` because each spawns its own bare DB; ignore unless directly touched.
- Test DB needs migrations: `direnv exec . env MIX_ENV=test mix ecto.create && mix ecto.migrate`.
- `mix precommit` (alias) runs `compile --warnings-as-errors`, `deps.unlock --unused`, `format`, `test`. Note: format will reformat unrelated files — split those into a separate "chore: mix format" commit before the feature commit.

**2. Commit**
- Lefthook pre-commit runs ast-grep, lint-grep, treefmt (`--fail-on-change`). Treefmt scans all files, so any unformatted file blocks the commit.
- Commit-msg uses conform (conventional commits). Prefix with `feat(scope):`, `fix(scope):`, `chore:` etc. Keep header under ~70 chars.

**3. Deploy**
- Push to GitHub master: `git push origin master` (the configs flake input is `github:ngngardner/readaloud`).
- In `/home/noah/projects/configs/`: `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix flake update readaloud` to bump the lock.
  - Note: the configs project's direnv shell does NOT include `nix` itself — call `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix` directly.
- Deploy: `cd /home/noah/projects/configs && /nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix develop --command bash -c "deploy --on pylon"`. The `deploy` shell command wraps `colmena apply --impure --on <hosts>`.
- Watch for `Activation successful` and `All done!` from pylon. The `readaloud.service` systemd unit gets restarted in the `starting the following units:` line.

**4. Verify**
- Smoke: `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://pylon:4000/` should return 200.
- Browser: use Claude-in-Chrome MCP against `http://pylon:4000/`.

**Browser verification recipe (Claude-in-Chrome MCP):**
1. `tabs_context_mcp createIfEmpty=true` once to get a `tabId` (and create a tab if none exists).
2. `browser_batch` for chained navigate + screenshot — saves round-trips.
3. To click DaisyUI dropdown triggers (`<div tabindex="0" role="button">`), use `find` to get a ref then `computer left_click ref=...`. Coordinate clicks on these can miss focus and the popover won't open.
4. To pick a `<select>` value, prefer `form_input` (works reliably **when the select is inside a `<form>` tag**). For phx-change selects rendered outside a form, form serialization is broken — but that's a code bug to fix (wrap in `<form phx-change=... phx-submit=...>`), not a test workaround.
5. `find query="..."` returns refs and (when the select is closed) lists its option text in the description — handy for asserting voice/model lists without opening the dropdown.

**Useful queries:**
- Books with audio activated: `SELECT id, title, audio_preferences FROM books WHERE audio_preferences IS NOT NULL`
- Books without audio (good for testing Set up audio): `SELECT id, title FROM books WHERE audio_preferences IS NULL LIMIT 5`
- DB path on pylon: `/var/lib/readaloud/data/readaloud.db`
- Service: `systemctl status readaloud` on pylon (root@pylon SSH).
- LocalAI URL the running service uses: `systemctl show readaloud.service --property=Environment | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -i localai`
